reasons: Both handle the 10-digit check correctly, but A also uses the correct weights for the 11th digit and gets only the 12th-digit weights wrong, while B uses wrong weights for both 12-digit control digits, so B rejects nearly every real individual INN. Both include tests for both lengths and the invalid inputs, but their 12-digit 'valid' examples are unverified and probably fail. Both claim HIGH confidence without grounds.

A: 12th-digit weights given as 7,2,4,10,3,5,9,4,6,8,1; the correct weights are 3,7,2,4,10,3,5,9,4,6,8
Test INN 772612345678 is claimed valid without verification and likely fails
The hand-check of 7707083893 lists the wrong digit sequence
B: 11th-digit weights given as 2,4,10,3,5,9,4,6,8,9; the correct weights are 7,2,4,10,3,5,9,4,6,8
12th-digit weights given as 2,4,10,3,5,9,4,6,8,9,10; the correct weights are 3,7,2,4,10,3,5,9,4,6,8
Claims the 12-digit test INN was manually checked, which is unsupported
